correctness.rationale: Total domination of KG(n,2) is equivalent to an auxiliary selected-edge graph having vertex cover number at least three; deletion minimality forces cover number exactly three and all edge deletions coverable by two vertices. For each selected edge an opposing two-cover produces pairs of 2-sets satisfying the disjointness/cross-intersection condition, and the elementary random-order two-families inequality yields at most six selected edges. The source six-edge isolate-free unlabeled graph generator was inspected: inductive one-edge extensions exhaust all graphs of <=6 edges, followed by exact cover/isomorphism tests, identifying precisely 3K2, K3 disjoint K2, C5, K4. Support label counts give 15 C(n,6), 10 C(n,5), 12 C(n,5), C(n,4) at sizes 3,4,5,6. Independently tested direct total domination of KG(n,2) for n=4,5,6; agrees. Not using finite orders as proof of all n.

originality.rationale: Prior Resultary full-text all-minimal ORDINARY dominating KG(n,2) classification allows triangles, stars, double-stars etc and uses closed-neighborhood domination. Total domination requires even chosen vertices have neighbors, equivalently no 2-cover whatsoever. The prior theorem is not equivalent and cannot imply the submitted four-type and inclusion-minimal TOTAL enumerator. Brešar–Cornet–Dravec–Henning establish total-domination minimum/extremal facts and Cornet–Torres closed k-tuple bounds, not this four-type complete inclusion-minimal census in inspected accessible material.
